adaptations.changed_behavior: In hybrid_common/4 only, concatenate the raw binary returned by crypto:compute_key(ecdh,...,x25519) with the post-quantum secret before the existing SHA-256 operation. Remove the lossy integer-to-SSH-mpint-and-last32 reconstruction from the hybrid path.
adaptations.rationale: The pinned generic compute_key/4 converts the raw 32-byte X25519 result to an unsigned integer. ssh_bits:mpint/1 then emits a minimal signed integer plus a 4-byte length. When a raw secret starts 0x00 and its next byte is below 0x80, its minimal content is shorter than 32 bytes; taking the last 32 bytes can incorporate the mpint length field. The deterministic example 000102...1f becomes1f0102...1f, so the hybrid KDF hashes different bytes. Keeping the original crypto binary avoids this conversion while preserving crypto validation/errors. Independent byte/ladders and actual installed Crypto evidence confirm this defect. Two old-runtime raw failures are preserved, and the private corrected helper passes identical assertions in both runtimes. The rebuilt product now passes the installed regression in ordinary, relocated and producer-isolated bounded checks. Full SSH and external interoperability remain pending.
